title: Claim Evidence Verification Became a Mechanical Runtime Boundary
summary: A deterministic Claim → Evidence → Verification runtime was added so VERIFIED cannot be a model assertion, memory assertion, user assertion, or stale result; evidence is tied to the commit it observed and adversarial CI tests the boundary.
what_happened: The next load-bearing enforcement slice after Restore Context was implemented with a standard-library runtime, ten adversarial unit tests, a CI workflow that generates current-commit evidence, validates it, verifies a claim, and publishes machine-readable evidence.
what_we_learned: Verification must be derived from observed evidence rather than status labels or model confidence.
Evidence freshness must be bound to the commit under verification; historical evidence cannot silently prove changed current state.
Adversarial tests must explicitly reject model, memory, user, and retrieved-content assertions as evidence-producing methods.
CI should emit machine-readable evidence tied to the exact checkout so green status can be reconstructed rather than merely remembered.
why_it_matters: This closes a critical gap between Naya remembering that something worked and Naya being able to prove that it worked on the exact system state being evaluated.
what_changed: Added Claim Evidence CI enforcement with exact-commit evidence generation and artifact publication.
Added evidence store README and canonical memory note.
next_best_action: Run the new Claim Evidence workflow, inspect every job and artifact, then use the verified evidence boundary as the substrate for independent Oscar challenge and promotion rules.
